title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.25-27): L is a totally ordered set, apparently with a smallest element σ and a largest element α. It may carry extra 'admissible' or tame structure; p.25 mentions 'admissibles'. A 'tronçon' is an interval of L of one of these types: [a,b], ]a,b], [a,b[, ]a,b[ (a<b), L_{≤a}, L_{≥a}, L_{<a} (a≠σ), L_{>a} (a≠α), or L itself. The 'absolute boundary' ∂T is the set of least and greatest elements of T. On p.25 he shows ∂T = (Ṫ∩T) ⨿ (T∩∂L), where Ṫ is the topological frontier. He also shows that every tronçon can be written uniquely as T∖α, with T a closed tronçon and α⊂∂T.

This page:
(1) Terminology. ]a,b[, L_{<a}, L_{>a} and L are called 'open'; these are exactly the intervals open in the canonical order topology. ]a,b] and [a,b[ are called 'semi-open'.
(2) Caveat. If a is the least element, then [a,b[ is semi-open in this terminology but open in the order topology, since it equals L_{<b}. The same happens at the other end. L is both open and closed.
(3) Pseudo-tronçons. A 'tronçon général' (later 'ps.-tronçon') is a subset of L that is either a point or a tronçon. For T' = T∖α (T closed, α⊂∂T) he decides to set ∂T' := ∂T, so the boundary of a pseudo-interval includes its missing endpoints. A crossed-out attempt reads ∂T' = T'∪∂L. A marginal remark observes that this boundary is not determined by T' with its induced order alone; it depends on how T' sits in L. In effect T' is the datum of an interval together with its endpoints-as-cuts.
(4) Definition. Two pseudo-tronçons T, T' are 'in tame relative position' (next page: 'position relative modérée') if ∂T and ∂T' are, i.e. if ∂T∪∂T' is totally ordered, presumably relative to some earlier notion. A marginal NB concerns ∂T ≠ ∅.

Purpose: p.27 proves that the intersection of two pseudo-tronçons in tame position is empty or a pseudo-tronçon, with ∂(T∩T') ⊂ ∂T∪∂T'. It then introduces the order T<T' and the strict relation T≪T', distinguishing 'raccordement' (gluing) positions where the intervals share an endpoint. This is groundwork in dimension 1 for 'réseaux via découpages', i.e. combinatorial cell decompositions in the spirit of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme.
errors: Taken literally, with L totally ordered, the condition 'ΔT∪ΔT′ totally ordered' is vacuous. The intended tameness condition must refer to an earlier notion (admissible/tame point sets) not visible on this page, or the definition is still being drafted.
The page writes 'L_{<a}, L_{>a}' as open without repeating the restrictions a≠σ, a≠α from p.25. This is harmless.
'∂T′ = T′ ∪ ∂L' is a discarded attempt and is not correct as a boundary formula. The adopted convention is ∂T′ := ∂T.

ideas.what: Classification of intervals in a bounded totally ordered set into open/semi-open/closed, compared with the order topology (endpoint caveat)
Pseudo-intervals: an interval together with its endpoints as 'cuts', with boundary not intrinsic to the induced order (depends on the embedding in L)
ideas.modern_name: Intervals with marked endpoints / cuts; boundary relative to ambient ordered set (as in o-minimal cell decomposition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; in tame setting van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimality, 1984–86)

ideas.what: 'Tame relative position' of pseudo-intervals, ensuring intersections are pseudo-intervals with boundary in the union of boundaries
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of 1-cells in a cell decomposition / stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal cell decomposition (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches tame topology only in outline; no such formal definitions published

missed.claim: This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a purely order-theoretic, combinatorial foundation for 'réseaux via découpages' (tame topology). It is built from intervals, boundaries and relative positions in a totally ordered set. The page itself is routine. The interest lies only in the overall axiomatic programme, which remains unpublished; this page contributes no new result.
missed.quote: Deux ps tronçons sont dits en pos. rel. modérée ... si ∂T et ∂T' le sont
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. Possibly of historical interest for comparison with o-minimal cell decomposition and combinatorial approaches to tame topology. Not mathematically new at this level.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary definitions about intervals in an ordered set and the order topology. It is preparatory material for a tame-topology programme, with no new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'sont dits en pos. ordinale modulaire ... (T,T') modulaire ... {T,T'} modulaire' should very likely read 'en pos. relative modérée ... (T,T') modérée ... {T,T'} modérée'. Page 27 uses 'position rel modérée'.
'et [b,a[ sont dits semi-ouverts' should be '[a,b[' (mirror of ]a,b]).
'{+ou pos. tronçons+}' should read 'ou ps.-tronçons' (pseudo-tronçons), an alternative name for 'tronçon général'.
'(T tronçon fermé, α∈∂T' is probably 'α⊂∂T', consistent with p.25 ('T∖α, avec α⊂∂T').
Right margin: likely 'Mais tiens, cela n'est pas déterminé par la donnée de T' par la structure d'ordre induite', i.e. ∂T' is not intrinsic to T' with its induced order.
'Idem idem ailleurs' probably 'Idem pour b ailleurs' / 'Idem si b plus grand élément' (the symmetric caveat at the upper end).
